faq.title: What everyone asks before the pilot.

items.q: Does it work with the cameras I already have?
items.a: It works with regular IP cameras: Intelbras, Hikvision and any ONVIF-compatible one. What matters is angle and light, and the specialist checks that with you before you start.

items.q: Do I need internet in the plant?
items.a: No, if processing runs on the device in the plant: the reading happens inside, without internet. In the cloud, the camera needs an outbound internet connection.
The cloud needs no hardware in the plant. The device in the plant keeps the video inside and does not depend on internet. The specialist helps you choose for your scenario.
We pick one or two cameras and a scenario, turn the reading on and follow the alerts with your team until the rule works the way the operation needs.
We monitor the condition (helmet, flame, posture), not the identity. Clip retention is set by contract.

meta.title: About Logikos

hero.question: who are we?
hero.title: Reason and sight.
hero.text: ΛΟΓΙΚΟΣ is Greek for rational. We are a team of born innovators who love technology, making the cameras industry already has understand what they see.

manifesto.title: Why we exist
manifesto.text: Every plant already has cameras, and almost nobody is looking at them when it matters. Logikos exists to turn that image into an alert for whoever decides: the early fire, the forgotten PPE, the out-of-spec part, with the proof attached.

vision.title: Computer vision, no mystery
vision.text: The camera stays the same. What changes is that a model trained by Logikos starts to understand what it sees and tells whoever needs to act. Industry 4.0 in practice: real-time operations data and faster decisions, without replacing what already works.

controller.title: Who handles your data
controller.text: Logikos Soluções, CNPJ {cnpj}, is the controller of the data sent through this website.

data.title: What we collect
data.text: Name, company, role, email, WhatsApp number, interests and the message you write in the form, plus technical data about the submission: IP address (used only for the anti-abuse check), page, language, date and time. This website uses no tracking or advertising cookies.

purpose.title: Why we use it
purpose.text: To answer your inquiry and follow up on the conversation you asked for.

legalBasis.title: Legal basis
legalBasis.text: Consent, recorded when you send the form (Brazil's LGPD, art. 7, I). Final basis under legal review.

sharing.title: Who we share it with
sharing.text: With Cloudflare, which hosts this website, stores inquiries and runs the anti-abuse check, acting as processor. Data may be processed outside Brazil, with the safeguards of LGPD art. 33. We do not sell data.

antiAbuse.title: Abuse protection
antiAbuse.text: The forms and the conversation with Koda are protected against bots by a hidden field and a per-network-address sending limit. No third-party service is called for it.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.text: For as long as the conversation lasts and for any period the law requires.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You can ask for confirmation of processing, access, correction, anonymization, blocking or deletion, portability and information about sharing, and withdraw consent at any time (LGPD, art. 18). You can also petition Brazil's data protection authority (ANPD).

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.text: This site uses no cookies. Your browser keeps only session records, so the home opening and the logo animation don’t repeat in the same visit and, if you arrived through a link in a Logikos e-mail, that e-mail’s code (no personal data). That code is sent to our team, only once, to record that the visit happened, only if you accept; without acceptance, the code never leaves your browser and is gone when the tab closes. If you accept later in the same visit, it is sent once; and your choice about audience measurement ("lk-consentimento": accepted or declined, with the date). Audience measurement (Cloudflare Web Analytics) is anonymous, uses no cookies and loads only if you accept. To change your choice at any time, use "Cookie preferences" in the footer of any page.

meta.title: Container yard — a Logikos case
meta.description: Computer vision scoped to record the arrival, the moves and the exact position of each container in the yard.

hero.title: Container yard.
hero.text: A container depot wants to know, without manual logging, when each container arrives, when it is moved and where it is right now. Logikos scoped the computer vision for it.

problem.title: Where is each container?
problem.text: Stacked containers, moved by forklifts and reach stackers, in an operation that may never stop. Finding a container by hand takes the team’s time and leaves room for error when releasing the cargo.

scope.title: From the gate to the stack.
scope.text: Every container has a unique code, and the camera reads it. At the gate, dedicated cameras record arrivals and departures; in the yard, others follow the moves. When the yard has no cameras yet, the project specifies and installs them.

points.title: Arrivals recorded
points.text: Each container’s arrival, with the code read and the frame as proof.

points.title: Moves followed
points.text: When a container changes place inside the yard.

points.title: Exact location
points.text: Each container’s slot and level in the stack, on a panel with its history.

extra.question: and the yard’s logistics?
extra.title: Logistics operations
extra.text: Knowing where each container is comes first. Next is deciding where it should go: placing loads by arrival and departure, so what leaves first stays easiest to reach.

points.title: Placement by departure order
points.text: Each incoming container gets a position planned for when it will leave, with no reshuffling of the stack.

points.title: Fewer moves
points.text: Fewer manoeuvres to pull a container from under others: the equipment works on what matters.

points.title: A faster yard
points.text: A more predictable flow from the gate to the stack, and cargo is released sooner.

meta.title: Augmented reality for logistics — a Logikos case
meta.description: Computer vision with augmented reality for picking and checking in logistics.

hero.title: Augmented reality for logistics.
hero.text: The camera recognizes what the operator is looking at, and the screen overlays the information they need at that moment.

problem.title: Search, check, write down.
problem.text: In picking and checking, much of the time goes into finding the right item and confirming it is the one. Every mistake becomes rework or a return.

scope.title: Information in the right place.
scope.text: We understand the process, the items and the equipment the team already uses. Then we define what the camera needs to recognize and what shows on screen.

points.title: The right item highlighted
points.text: The operator sees on screen where the item they need is.

points.title: Checking on the spot
points.text: The camera confirms the item before it moves on.

points.title: A record of each step
points.text: What was picked and checked, for management to follow.

extra.question: what does it look like in logistics?
extra.title: Guided picking in the warehouse
extra.text: With the order in hand, the operator doesn’t have to search. The screen shows where each product is and the best route through the warehouse to collect everything the order asks for.

points.title: Where the product is
points.text: The order’s item is highlighted on the right shelf.

points.title: The best route
points.text: Pick order follows the shortest path through the warehouse, based on the order.

points.title: Instant confirmation
points.text: The camera checks that the item picked is the one in the order before it moves on.

meta.title: Operations control — a Logikos case
meta.description: Computer vision to follow each step of the process and gather it on one panel.

hero.title: Operations control.
hero.text: The cameras already watching the process start telling you what is happening at each step, and management sees it all on one panel.

problem.title: What happens between one log entry and the next.
problem.text: Stops, queues and out-of-sequence steps usually show up only at the end of the shift, when it is too late to act.

scope.title: The steps that matter to you.
scope.text: We understand the process and the indicators management follows. Then we define what each camera reads, who gets each notice and how the data reaches your system.

points.title: Every step followed
points.text: What came in, what stopped and what went out, with the frame as proof.

points.title: A notice while there is time
points.text: When something strays from plan, whoever decides knows right away.

points.title: Your operation’s indicators
points.text: The numbers you already follow, fed by the cameras.

extra.question: where does it apply?
extra.title: Where it applies and what you follow
extra.text: It fits any operation split into steps the cameras can see: assembly and production lines, shipping and docks, warehouses and distribution centres, yards and maintenance areas.

points.title: Progress by step
points.text: What is at each step now, and what has already gone through it this shift.

points.title: Bottlenecks
points.text: Where work is piling up before it becomes a queue.

points.title: Stops
points.text: When a step stops, for how long and when it restarted.

points.title: Real-time alerts
points.text: Whoever decides is notified on the phone or the panel as soon as something strays from plan.

points.title: Shift indicators
points.text: The numbers management already follows, updated by the cameras throughout the shift.
